notes: Audit #2 Batch 1 «شکاف‌های PR1» (v1.11.68) — the first of the 5 approved batches of the v1.11.67 full audit (88/100, 0 Critical, 0 High). (1) M1 — stale-beacon guard: CORRECTION to the 1.11.67 notes: the claim that a stale beacon's day-flag/useful changes are dropped was true only for dict/list keys — patch_only let scalars (theme, lang, nextBoxRemind, telegramChatId) and nullables (assignments, exams, sim, usefulPrompt, lastErrorReview) pass through and overwrite NEWER values (live-confirmed by two independent audit inspectors: tab B saved theme=dark + an assignment; tab A's stale beacon with theme=light + assignments=null cleared them with HTTP 200). A stale beacon now applies ONLY the merged keys (done, tests, edits, actualMinutes, tests_total) + the activeTimer guards — new beacon_only mode on merge_state_update_scoped; scalars and nullables are ignored there too. The beacon's only job is rescuing the closing tab's ticks/minutes. Explicit partial POSTs keep the patch_only scalar exemption (the 1.11.64 telegramChatId live tests still pin that a partial scalar applies). (2) M2 — testbook tombstone: the 1.11.67 claim that the 1.11.61 caveat is resolved was WRONG for the beacon path — a stale beacon body still carries the deleted book, so the book-level merge resurrected it (live-confirmed: geom deleted via replace, stale beacon brought it back). A replace save now records the ids it deletes in testbook_tombstones.json (beside seq.json); the merge NEVER restores a tombstoned id — neither from disk nor from the stale body — and load_testbook restore paths (backup/seed/cloud) apply the same filter. A later replace save containing the id clears its tombstone (a deliberate re-add). No book-delete UI exists yet, so this was unreachable via UI — fixed anyway, before any such UI is built. (3) L1 — the testbook 409 response now reads the seq AFTER building the payload: load_testbook() may restore a corrupt file from backup and bump the counter, so the pre-load seq was stale and the client burned one of its 3 retries on a gratuitous extra 409 (live probe: the 409 carried seq 1 while the real counter was 2). The state path already ordered it this way. (4) L6 — adopt now sets the server counter to exactly the client value (was client+1, and the save's own bump then made it client+2 — a harmless but undocumented +2 jump per seq.json loss); the save's bump now makes it client+1. seq.json still holds both streams in one file, so losing it resets both counters at once (splitting into two files was considered and not done). (5) L20 — testbook save failures now mirror the state path (ب-7): a non-409 error, exhausted 409 retries, or a thrown fetch all show the toastNotSavedReason toast with a one-click retry calling runSaveTestbook() — not just the red saveFailed pill. KNOWN LIMIT (unchanged): same-box / same-book concurrent edits stay last-writer-wins. PROVEN by a two-tab jsdom harness (verify1168) + live-server driver + in-repo tests (TestAudit2Batch1_1168): the M1 live probe (stale beacon keeps the newer theme/assignment, ticks land), the M2 live probe (deleted geom stays gone through a stale beacon, re-add via replace clears the tombstone), the L1 probe (409 seq equals the post-restore counter), the L6 probe (adopt lands on client+1), and the L20 jsdom check (testbook save failure shows the toast with a working retry). Nothing deferred. i18n 1439/1439 (no new keys — L20 reuses the existing ب-7 toast).
